summary: Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is an indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from Freie Universität Berlin in 2000. He taught Andrea Schlosser and Kathrin Holz, and held a professorship at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).
Inyoung Chung specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Chung earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, and Paris-Sorbonne University, as well as under Mircea Eliade (~1975–1986). He held posts at Groningen and Chicago.
Iona Macgregor is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin (attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Toyo University (attested 2014) and Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and Sukumar Sen, served at Deccan College (~1939–1942), and was Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

Irawati Karve (1905–1970) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Fergusson College, Huzurpaga, and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

Irfan Habib (born 1931) is an Indian historian and indologist. He studied at Minto Circle, Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953), and New College (~1954–1957), and served as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1953 to 1994.

Irving Babbitt (1865–1933) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Harvard College, Harvard University, Williams College, and the University of Paris. Babbitt taught Yongtong Tang and Wu Mi, holding posts at Williams and Harvard.

Isaac Schapera (1905–2003) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and London School of Economics, and taught Bridget Allchin. He held posts at the LSE (~1950–1969), Chicago (~1953–1954), and Toronto (~1961–1962).

Isaak Jakob Schmidt (1779–1847) was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Rostock. He held posts with the Russian Bible Society and the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences/Russian Academy of Sciences.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at Université libre de Bruxelles, Tibet University, Harvard, and EPHE under Fernand Meyer and Françoise Lauwaert. She held posts teaching anthropology at Laval University (~2004, 2007).

Isabelle Ratié (born 1976) specializes in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Paris 1 and EPHE under Lyne Bansat-Boudon and Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at Leipzig, Sorbonne Nouvelle (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).

Isaiah Berlin (1909–1997) was a philosopher and historian. He was educated at St Paul's School and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and held a post at the University of Oxford from around 1932 to 1975.

Isaline Blew Horner (1896–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. She studied under Caroline Rhys Davids and at Newnham College and Cambridge. She served at Newnham, Cambridge, and held long-term secretary roles at the Pali Text Society.
Isamu Kanaji (1919–1988) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Attested in 1976, he held posts as professor at Shitennoji University and International Buddhist University Junior College.

Isao Nishitani works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Nishitani held posts at Sennyu-ji (attested 2016) and as an associate professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2026).

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Attested in 2016, she held positions as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820–1891) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He held posts at Fort William College, Sanskrit College, and served as director at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
